map.title: Urdaibai — Listening-informed systems map
map.question: What helps or hinders people staying in Urdaibai while sustaining the local economy and preserving the territory?
map.description: A synthesis proposed from ten supplied interview documents, completed with explicit modeller hypotheses. It is not a validated shared mental model.

provenance_legend.interview: Relationship or idea described in interviews; interview-level references, not a quote audit.
provenance_legend.hypothesis: Modeller-added mechanism, not established by the interview evidence.

limitations: No participant or independent linguistic validation.
No systematic quote-level support or contradiction audit.
Some variable definitions aggregate distinct mechanisms.
Tourism is an external driver; ecosystems have no outgoing influence.
Map polarity is not a CIB state-to-state score.

variables.name: Tourism activity
variables.definition: Intensity of visitor activity in the territory, including day visits and overnight stays.
variables.review_notes: This variable is an external driver in version 0.1. Visitor volume is not the same as economic benefit.

variables.name: Locally retained economic benefits
variables.definition: Economic benefits reaching residents and local organisations through earnings, procurement and other income.
variables.review_notes: Broadened from tourism benefits to benefits from local initiatives. This generalisation requires review; distribution is not represented separately.

variables.name: Access to permanent housing
variables.definition: Residents’ ability to obtain year-round housing at costs compatible with their income.
variables.review_notes: Availability and affordability are aggregated in this first version.

variables.name: Ecosystem condition
variables.definition: Health of habitats and ecosystems, including wetlands.
variables.review_notes: An outcome-only variable in this map; ecological feedback is not represented.

variables.name: Access to essential services
variables.definition: Ability to meet everyday needs for health, care and basic services, including the travel required.
variables.review_notes: Aggregates different services and mobility. They may evolve in different directions.

variables.name: Stable local employment
variables.definition: Availability of local paid work with continuity across the year.
variables.review_notes: More economic activity does not automatically create stable or adequately paid jobs.

variables.name: Young adults staying locally
variables.definition: Extent to which young adults remain resident in the territory.
variables.review_notes: Retention is not identical to net migration or the size of the resident population. Age range remains to be defined.

variables.name: Year-round local demand
variables.definition: Demand from residents for locally supplied goods and services throughout the year.
variables.review_notes: Modeller-added mechanism, informed by the discussion of spending outside the region in interview 0105.

variables.name: Viability of local businesses
variables.definition: Ability of businesses serving local demand to sustain operations.
variables.review_notes: Applies primarily to locally oriented retail and services, not equally to export businesses.

variables.name: Trust in collective action
variables.definition: Expectation that working together can produce credible and fairly distributed local outcomes.
variables.review_notes: Distinct from trust in institutional decisions. The change of meaning from the earlier discussion needs review.

variables.name: Territorial coordination
variables.definition: Ability of municipalities, institutions, firms and civil society to organise joint action at regional scale.
variables.review_notes: Coordination is a capacity, not a guarantee of desirable outcomes.

variables.name: Delivery of joint initiatives
variables.definition: Extent to which jointly organised initiatives are implemented.
variables.review_notes: Type, purpose and distribution of initiatives matter; implementation alone does not ensure benefits.

influences.explanation: Visitor activity can generate income for local accommodation, businesses and workers.
influences.conditions: Visitors spend locally and benefits are retained rather than leaking out.
influences.review_notes: Not all visitor growth benefits residents.

influences.explanation: Tourism growth can encourage conversion to short-term accommodation and restrict access to year-round housing.
influences.conditions: Housing supply and regulation do not offset conversion or price pressure.
influences.review_notes: The effect is mediated by the accommodation and housing markets.

influences.explanation: Visitor pressure and associated infrastructure can damage habitats and ecosystems.
influences.conditions: Activity affects vulnerable locations without sufficient protection or mitigation.
influences.review_notes: A perceived causal mechanism, not an independently verified ecological effect.

influences.explanation: Additional visitors place demands on transport, waste and other local services.
influences.conditions: Service capacity and municipal resources do not keep pace.
influences.review_notes: The interview describes resource pressure; the map generalises to access.

influences.explanation: Locally retained benefits may sustain businesses and create continuing employment.
influences.conditions: Benefits are invested in year-round activity rather than only rents or seasonal jobs.
influences.review_notes: Requires review; retained income is not a sufficient condition for stable jobs.

influences.explanation: Local work makes it more practicable for young adults to remain resident.
influences.conditions: Work is suitable and other necessities, including housing, are accessible.
influences.review_notes: Employment is one influence among several.

influences.explanation: Accessible year-round housing makes remaining in the territory more feasible.
influences.conditions: Housing is suitable for residents’ circumstances.
influences.review_notes: Does not imply housing alone determines migration.

influences.explanation: Access to everyday services may make staying locally more feasible and attractive.
influences.conditions: Services meet needs relevant to young adults and their households.
influences.review_notes: Specific services and their importance remain unresolved.

influences.explanation: Retained young residents may sustain regular local spending.
influences.conditions: Residents have purchasing power and spend a meaningful share locally.
influences.review_notes: Retention is a proxy; population, income and spending location are omitted mediators.

influences.explanation: Regular local demand may help locally oriented firms cover costs and remain viable.
influences.conditions: Demand reaches these firms and margins are sufficient.
influences.review_notes: Primarily concerns local retail and services.

influences.explanation: Viable local firms may retain or create continuing jobs.
influences.conditions: Business survival or growth translates into stable paid work.
influences.review_notes: Employment intensity and working conditions are not fixed.

influences.explanation: Trust in working together can make sustained cooperation easier.
influences.conditions: Actors have opportunities and authority to cooperate.
influences.review_notes: Interpretive synthesis; institutional trust and interpersonal trust are not interchangeable.

influences.explanation: Coordination can bring decisions, resources and capabilities together to implement initiatives.
influences.conditions: Coordination has resources and effective decision-making capacity.
influences.review_notes: Some interview statements are proposed remedies rather than observed causal outcomes.

influences.explanation: Joint initiatives may generate economic benefits that remain locally.
influences.conditions: Initiatives address local needs and benefits are retained locally.
influences.review_notes: Not every initiative has an economic objective or produces positive results.

influences.explanation: Visible local benefits may strengthen confidence in collective action.
influences.conditions: Benefits are recognised as fair and credibly attributed to joint action.
influences.review_notes: Economic benefit alone does not guarantee trust.

influences.explanation: Joint initiatives can improve essential-service access.
influences.conditions: Initiatives specifically address services and are effective.
influences.review_notes: A conditional pathway, not a generic effect of all initiatives.

loops.name: Everyday economy
loops.narrative: Stable employment supports staying locally. Residents sustain year-round demand, helping local businesses remain viable and sustain jobs. The same reinforcing structure can amplify decline or recovery.
loops.review_notes: Three of four links are modeller hypotheses. This cycle is not demonstrated by the interviews.

loops.name: Collective capacity
loops.narrative: Trust supports coordination and delivery of joint initiatives. When these produce visible, fairly distributed local benefits, trust may increase.
loops.review_notes: Two closing links are modeller hypotheses. Delivery without recognised and fairly distributed benefits need not build trust.

presentation.label: Analyst synthesis · exploratory, unvalidated
presentation.note: Previously authored influence-map synthesis. Model hypotheses and loops dependent on them are optional. Interview-level references are not quotation-level validation. Do not generate new links to connect the evidence layers.
